transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. This work requires specialized equipment and certification to handle gases properly without risking injury or damage to the appliance. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the sealed cooling system or its controls. Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?
no the freezer is warm too, about 0C and everything's thawed. fridge about 13C. no ice on the back wall at all, no frost anywhere. compressor runs non-stop though
From what you have described, the most likely cause is the automatic defrost system. Behind the rear panel inside the freezer, are the coils a solid block of ice, or fairly clear?
i havent taken the back panel off, but theres no frost anywhere inside, freezer back wall isnt even cold. can hear a fan going when the door's shut though

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the sealed cooling system or its controls. Fridge freezers lose their heat through a coil or grille at the back or underneath. Gently dust or vacuum it, and leave a few centimetres of space between it and the wall or cupboards. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space round it?
not sure, haven't pulled it out to look. its only barely warm at the back, not hot like it used to be. the rating plate says R600a on it if that matters

The first step is a full manual defrost: switch it off at the socket, move the food into cool bags, put towels down and leave the doors open until every bit of ice has melted, then dry it and switch it back on. Have you been able to do a full defrost, or is there no ice to clear?

there's no ice to clear, everything's already thawed and no frost anywhere. havent done a full defrost though, should i do that anyway? and theres a bit of an oily mark on the pipe near the compressor if that helps

Yes, you should perform a full defrost as it is a safe and standard troubleshooting step for this symptom. Ensure the appliance is unplugged during the process to avoid any electrical hazards. When you press the freezer door switch, do you hear the fan running, and are the coils clear or iced up?
i can hear the fan going with the door shut, not sure about pressing the door switch. havent got the back panel off so cant see the coils. ok ill do the defrost then, will that sort it?

Defrosting is unlikely to fix this because there is no frost buildup and both compartments are warm. The symptoms point to a refrigerant leak or compressor failure rather than an ice blockage. Run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
ok ill check the seals, but they looked fine last time i noticed. do you reckon its the compressor then? whats the cheapest way to sort it, its out of warranty

It is unlikely to be just the compressor since there are no signs of frost and the system has been running non-stop without cooling. The oily mark on the pipe suggests a refrigerant leak, which requires professional repair by a qualified engineer due to safety regulations regarding R600a gas. Keep both doors shut for about 24 hours (only open them briefly) and let it recover. After a day with the doors shut, is it back to cold, or still warm?
